survey: A stone chess/checkers table in a park. A thick square stone tabletop with an inset checkerboard of raised dark and cream tiles in a regular alternating pattern, facing up and tilted toward the camera. The top sits centered on one square stone pedestal. The pedestal stands on a wide, thin stone base slab that lies flat on the grass, with grass growing around its edges. Two round stone stools, each a cylinder with a slightly wider cap, stand on the grass: one behind the table at the left and one in front at the right. Both have contact shadows and do not touch or pass through the table or the slab. The cracks are surface detail only. The board looks to have fewer than 8×8 squares, but at this size I couldn't count them exactly. I read it as a game-art simplification, like three buttons on a phone, not a construction fault. Everything rests on something, nothing floats, and the object could work as a park game table.
